commands.name: projector
commands.description: Show or hide Projector’s panel of your loops’ pull requests and your inbox
commands.output: Showing Projector’s panel above the prompt.

tools.name: ask
tools.description: Ask the person a question without stopping: it appears in Projector’s panel above their prompt, and you keep working. Ask in one short line of at most 120 characters, and put what they need to decide in `detail`. Always recommend an answer, and write it and each option as a full answer they can pick as it stands. Name the pull request the question is about in `pr`, as owner/repo#number. Keep working on anything the answer does not block. The call returns the question’s number, such as 3. When the person picks an option, a message that starts `ANSWER 3.<letter>` arrives later, or `DISMISSED 3` when they dismiss it. When they restore a question after you heard `DISMISSED 3`, `RESTORED 3` arrives, and the question is open again. When they reply in their own words instead, the reply arrives as their prompt, quoting the question, and the question stays open: answer what they asked, then withdraw the question if the reply settles it, revise it if it was unclear or the choice has changed, or leave it open while it still needs them. The panel never shows an item’s number, so name the item to the person by what it asks or tells, never by its number.

tools.name: tell
tools.description: Tell the person something without stopping: it appears in Projector’s panel above their prompt until they dismiss it. Use it for the answer to a question they asked you, or for something you did that they should know about. Write one short line of at most 120 characters, and put the rest in `detail`. Name the pull request it is about in `pr`, as owner/repo#number. Nothing comes back to you; when you need the person to decide something, use `ask` instead. The panel never shows an item’s number, so name the item to the person by what it asks or tells, never by its number.

tools.name: withdraw
tools.description: Withdraw a question or notice you posted that no longer needs the person, such as a question their reply settled or news that has gone stale. Name it by the number `ask` or `tell` returned. It leaves Projector’s panel at once. Nothing comes back to you: a withdrawn question sends no `DISMISSED` message. The panel never shows an item’s number, so name the item to the person by what it asks or tells, never by its number.

tools.name: revise
tools.description: Revise a question you asked that is still open, keeping its number, when the person’s reply shows it was unclear or the choice has changed. Name it by the number `ask` returned, and give only what changes: the question, its detail, the recommendation, or the other options, which `options` replaces as a whole. Projector’s panel redraws it at once, and its answer still arrives as a message that starts `ANSWER 3.<letter>` or `DISMISSED 3`. The panel never shows an item’s number, so name the item to the person by what it asks or tells, never by its number.

tools.name: restore
tools.description: Restore a question or notice you posted that the person dismissed or snoozed: it reopens in Projector’s panel under the same number, with the same text. Use it only when the person says a dismissal was a mistake or asks for the item back, never on your own judgement, and never ask a dismissed question again as a new one. Name it by the number `ask` or `tell` returned. A restored question’s answer arrives as before, as a message that starts `ANSWER 3.<letter>` or `DISMISSED 3`. The panel never shows an item’s number, so name the item to the person by what it asks or tells, never by its number.
